title: Ellingham thermodynamic logic
basic_overview: Oxide-formation ΔG° versus temperature helps decide whether a reductant can reduce a metal oxide.

extra_info_content.short_trick: Reductant must have stronger oxide-forming tendency under the conditions.
extra_info_content.step_by_step: 1. Write oxidation reactions. 2. Compare ΔG° lines. 3. Check relative position. 4. Consider temperature and phases.
extra_info_content.factors: Ellingham is thermodynamic; it does not by itself give the reaction rate.
extra_info_content.kinetics_or_energy: Compare thermodynamic driving force with kinetic barrier when relevant; do not treat a favourable ΔG° as proof of a fast reaction.
